subject: Custody & provenance: scrub acceptance criteria and rollback conditions
messages:
From: compliance@novacorp.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: evidence of EU custody + scrub acceptance criteria

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the call this morning. To close our procurement checklist we need the following items tied to the Dedicated deployment you proposed:

- Clear evidence the tenant is pinned to eu-west-1 (physical host locality and snapshot retention map)
- What parts of backups/snapshots are replicated off-region and what are the short/long term retention windows
- A concrete deletion/scrub acceptance criteria (how customer can be sure data is unrecoverable) including timeline and any forensic artifacts we should expect
- Escalation/rollback conditions: if a rollback is requested (legal hold / court order) how do you isolate and what are the timelines for reattaching a tenant to a restored snapshot in-region only

Could you provide artifacts or a playbook we can attach to our security review?

Best,
Marta Alvarez
Senior Compliance Manager
NovaCorp

---
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: compliance@novacorp.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence of EU custody + scrub acceptance criteria

Hi Marta,

Thanks — I pulled together a short pack and an ops playbook that covers the items you listed. Attached: redwood_region_provenance_v1.2.pdf (region binding evidence) and erase-playbook-appendix.zip (ops runbooks + sample audit logs). High-level summary below, and I copied Laura and Ben to confirm the SLA nuances.

1) Region pinning: customer tenants for Dedicated are pinned to a named VPC and a named host pool in eu-west-1. That mapping is recorded in our control plane and snap lineage is stored in an append-only provenance ledger (hash + timestamp). We can export the ledger slices for the tenant for audit.

2) Snapshots & backups: automated hourly snapshots retained for 14 days in-region; daily snapshots retained for 90 days in-region. Replication to a geo-archive is opt-in and disabled by default for Dedicated customers requiring strict residency. If replication had been enabled, the export shows explicit opt-in flags and replication targets.

3) Scrub acceptance criteria: we define "scrub complete" as: (a) tenant KV and active L2 caches zeroed, (b) all live volumes tombstoned and queued for secure wipe, (c) snapshot lineage removed from active catalog and tombstoned. Evidence artifacts we provide: wipe job logs, storage-firmware confirmation ID, and provenance ledger entries with tombstone markers and TTL expiry. Typical scrub completion for a tenant (no replication) is 72 hours after request; secure wipe confirmation from host vendor completes within 7 days depending on hardware HSM scheduling.

4) Rollback / legal hold: requests first create an immutable hold token in the control plane. While the hold is active, no automated scrub runs. Isolating the tenant is done by network ACLs + control-plane routing policies; reattach from a restored in-region snapshot typically takes 2–6 hours (depends on data size and warmup). If a rollback requires cross-region recovery we only perform that after an explicit documented escalation with legal sign-off.

I'll let Laura confirm the formal acceptance language for the procurement artifact, and Ben to confirm runbook ownership and timing SLAs.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_region_provenance_v1.2.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: erase-playbook-appendix.zip (zip)

---
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: compliance@novacorp.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence of EU custody + scrub acceptance criteria

Hi Marta / Rafael,

Thanks for sharing Rafael's summary. A few clarifications from a policy standpoint:

- We can provide signed, timebound attestation artifacts that indicate the tenant was pinned to eu-west-1 for a given window. These attestations include ledger hashes and the control-plane manifest. They are suitable for procurement and internal audit.
- For the scrub acceptance definition, recommend we add a short customer-facing checklist item: customer receives (i) wipe job id, (ii) storage vendor confirmation id, (iii) scrub completion timestamp. That checklist is what NovaCorp can mark as "accepted".
- We will not enable cross-region replication unless explicitly requested in writing by authorized NovaCorp admins.

Two items to confirm with you, Marta: is the 72-hour scrub window acceptable, and do you want us to produce a signed attestation at contract signature or after onboarding?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Trust & Policy | Redwood Inference

---
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com, compliance@novacorp.com
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence of EU custody + scrub acceptance criteria

Marta — operational notes:

- The 72-hour scrub window assumes no queued snapshots from archival replication. If archive replication was previously enabled and needs to be scrubbed, that adds a negotiation step with the archive target and can extend to 14 days.
- We will include a sample forensic artifact (example wipe job log) in the appendix. That file demonstrates the erase pass and storage-firmware confirmation lines.
- For rollback timelines: warm restores for typical Dedicated tenants (200–600GB) are about 2–3 hours; larger tenants (multi-TB) required staged warmup and we estimate up to 12 hours. We'll include sample warmup run durations in the playbook.

I'll own the scrub run and provide a primary ops contact for the execution window. Rafael — please include the contact in the SOW.

Ben Carter
Platform Ops Lead | Redwood Inference

From: compliance@novacorp.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence of EU custody + scrub acceptance criteria

Thanks — that level of detail helps. Quick answers:

- 72 hours is acceptable for our baseline; the 14-day extension for archive replication is also fine (we will not opt-in to replication in the initial contract).
- We would prefer the signed attestation at contract signature so it can be stored in our vendor file, but also receiving a runtime ledger slice after onboarding is useful for operational evidence.

Can you confirm the exact artifact names we should expect in the onboarding package so our procurement team can reconcile? Also, please provide the contact for Ben's ops lead.

Regards,
Marta Alvarez
Senior Compliance Manager | NovaCorp
